games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which reply disagrees politely and gives a reason?
choices: I disagree with everything you said.
I see your point, but I think that the cat would notice more, because animals watch food.
That is wrong and you know it.
No, the hero's view is the only one.
rounds.answer: I see your point, but I think that the cat would notice more, because animals watch food.
rounds.explanation: It names the other view, states its own view and supplies a reason. The other replies dismiss the speaker or omit a reason.

rounds.prompt: A narrator who uses the words I, me and my is telling a story in which point of view?
rounds.answer: First person
rounds.explanation: First-person narration uses I, me and my. Third person uses he, she and they, while tense and direct speech describe other features.

rounds.prompt: Choose the missing word from The Forgotten Mural, part 3: 'It belongs to the whole ______.'
rounds.answer: continent
rounds.explanation: Amal is saying the mural belongs to far more than one school, so she names the whole landmass.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: In Omar's account, how many days did the fishing boats come back with nothing?
choices: The fishing boats came back with nothing for nine days.
Amal says the fish eyes looked like tiny glass marbles.
It suggests the streets were wide and open, unlike the narrow lanes of their quiet village.
rounds.answer: The fishing boats came back with nothing for nine days.
rounds.explanation: Omar states the length of the empty spell directly in his second sentence.

rounds.prompt: What did the class decide to do straight after Teacher Yasmin praised their presentation?
choices: Amal says the fish eyes looked like tiny glass marbles.
The flag matches no real country, so Daniel decided it must stand for a group's own dream.
They voted to paint a new mural on their own school wall.
rounds.answer: They voted to paint a new mural on their own school wall.
rounds.explanation: The vote follows the praise and the news that saving the old mural was impractical.

rounds.prompt: Daniel says the flag on the tunic may stand for an early independence group. What made him think so?
choices: She promised that their mural would appear in the heritage newsletter.
The flag matches no real country, so Daniel decided it must stand for a group's own dream.
She asked them to investigate a hidden mural behind a wooden wall in the old federal hall.
rounds.answer: The flag matches no real country, so Daniel decided it must stand for a group's own dream.
rounds.explanation: He reasons from an absence of evidence: no country owns those colours, so the flag is symbolic.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: Choose the missing word from The Forgotten Mural, part 1: 'The centre was loud and ______, the opposite of their quiet village lanes.'
rounds.answer: spacious
rounds.explanation: The urban centre is contrasted with narrow village lanes, so the missing word describes open, roomy streets.

rounds.prompt: Which of these sentences is an opinion rather than a fact?
choices: Amal's account is far more exciting than Omar's.
The fishing boats returned empty for nine days.
Omar sells fish at a market stall.
The market stands near the coast.
rounds.answer: Amal's account is far more exciting than Omar's.
rounds.explanation: More exciting is a judgement that a reader could reasonably dispute. The other three can be checked against the texts.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses an opinion phrase correctly?
choices: In my opinion that the mural should stay.
I think the that mural should stay.
I believe that the mural should stay.
I feel that cold about the mural.
rounds.answer: I believe that the mural should stay.
rounds.explanation: In my opinion takes a comma, that never follows the article, and I feel drops that before a physical feeling.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: Which word names a large picture painted straight onto a wall?
rounds.answer: mural
rounds.explanation: A journal is a private notebook, a festival is a public event and a continent is a landmass, so only mural names wall art.

rounds.prompt: What does the word 'rural' describe?
choices: Belonging to the countryside, not the city.
A time when one country controlled another country.
A large event with music, food and shared activities.
A book for private daily writing.
rounds.answer: Belonging to the countryside, not the city.
rounds.explanation: Rural describes countryside places. The other options define colonial, festival and journal.

rounds.prompt: Choose the missing word from Omar's account: 'My ______ dried up like a puddle in the midday sun.'
rounds.answer: income
rounds.explanation: Omar is describing money that stopped arriving during the nine empty days, so income fits the sentence.
